title: Every ALM fund movement is gated by three independent checks: the RELAYER role, an isActive contract flag, and a rate limit
content:
The deposit and withdraw process definitions state the guards in the function signature itself. A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.2.1.3.1.1: "Only the `RELAYER` role is allowed to `depositAave`. Also, they must ensure the contract `isActive` i.e. can process the request", shown as `function depositAave(address aToken, uint256 amount) external onlyRole(RELAYER) isActive`. The withdrawal path (.3.2.1) repeats it verbatim for `withdrawAave`.

A third guard sits alongside: the operator "must ensure the `deposit` amount is allowed within the `RateLimits`", implemented as a `rateLimited(RateLimitHelpers.makeAssetKey(LIMIT_AAVE_DEPOSIT, aToken), amount)` modifier (.3.1.3), with the mirrored `LIMIT_AAVE_WITHDRAW` key on the withdraw side (.3.2.3).

The three guards fail independently and that is the point. `onlyRole(RELAYER)` answers *who*; `isActive` is a system-wide kill switch answering *whether the system should be moving at all*; the rate limit answers *how much*. An attacker holding the relayer key still faces a per-asset amount ceiling and can be halted globally by flipping `isActive` without needing to revoke keys.

The design consequence is that the Relayer can be a relatively hot, frequently-used operational role rather than a high-ceremony one. Its blast radius is bounded by parameters that governance sets, so operational convenience and custody risk are decoupled — the standard justification for putting throughput limits in code rather than in policy.
description: depositAave and withdrawAave both carry onlyRole(RELAYER) and isActive modifiers plus a rateLimited check, so compromising the operator key alone does not grant unbounded movement of capital.
